text.p: Allstate Corp said property-liability revenues rose 2.8 percent in fourth-quarter 1996, driven by increases in earned premiums and realized capital gains.
Property-liability revenues for the 1995 fourth quarter include revenues generated by commercial and reinsurance operations sold in the third quarter of 1996.
Personal lines written premium grew 5.3 percent to $4.50 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Operating income for fourth-quarter 1996 rose 38.7 percent to $430 million versus $310 million for the same 1995 period.
The improved property-liability performance was primarily due to favorable loss experience, including lower catastrophe losses, and premium growth.
After-tax catastrophe losses were $114 million for the period compared with $148 million for 1995.
Realized capital gains increased to $85 million after-tax, compared with $29 million for the same period in 1995.
